title: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP)
subject: haematology-oncology
summary: Suspect TTP in microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia with severe thrombocytopenia; send ADAMTS13 before treatment, use the PLASMIC score, start urgent plasma exchange with corticosteroids, add rituximab and caplacizumab where available, and avoid platelet transfusion unless bleeding is life-threatening.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia (schistocytes, raised LDH, low haptoglobin, raised indirect bilirubin and reticulocytes, DAT negative) with thrombocytopenia, often below 30 x 10^9/L.
Often with fluctuating neurological signs (confusion, headache, focal deficits, seizures), abdominal pain, fever or mild renal impairment. The full classic pentad is uncommon: do not wait for it.
Diagnosis is confirmed by ADAMTS13 activity below 10 IU/dL (10%) with an inhibitor or anti-ADAMTS13 antibody in immune TTP.

Differentials: DIC (abnormal clotting), HUS (prominent AKI), sepsis, malignant hypertension, pre-eclampsia or HELLP, drug-induced TMA (quinine, gemcitabine, calcineurin inhibitors), SLE and antiphospholipid syndrome.
In India also consider falciparum malaria, leptospirosis, dengue and Russell's viper envenomation, which can mimic TTP.

sections.title: Investigations and PLASMIC score
items: Take a sample for ADAMTS13 activity and inhibitor or antibody BEFORE plasma exchange or plasma infusion.

FBC, blood film for schistocytes, reticulocytes, LDH, haptoglobin, bilirubin, DAT, PT, APTT and fibrinogen (usually normal in TTP), renal and liver function, troponin and ECG (cardiac involvement), pregnancy test, HIV, hepatitis B and C serology, blood cultures and a malaria test.

PLASMIC score, 1 point each: platelets below 30 x 10^9/L; haemolysis (reticulocytes above 2.5%, undetectable haptoglobin, or indirect bilirubin above 2 mg/dL); no active cancer; no solid organ or stem cell transplant; MCV below 90 fL; INR below 1.5; creatinine below 2.0 mg/dL.
PLASMIC 6 to 7: high probability of severe ADAMTS13 deficiency; 5: intermediate; 0 to 4: low. Use it alongside clinical judgement, not instead of ADAMTS13.
CT or MRI brain if neurological features.

sections.title: Immediate management
items: Medical emergency: involve haematology at once and transfer to a centre with plasma exchange capability. Start plasma exchange without waiting for ADAMTS13 when clinical probability is high.

Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) daily using FFP or solvent-detergent plasma, 1.5 plasma volumes initially then 1.0 plasma volume daily, continued until platelet count recovers under haematology guidance. If TPE will be delayed, give plasma infusion as a bridge, watching for volume overload.
Corticosteroids with TPE (ISTH strong recommendation): methylprednisolone 1 g IV daily for 3 days, or prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day orally, then taper.
Rituximab added to TPE and steroids for first episodes and relapses (ISTH conditional): 375 mg/m2 IV weekly for 4 doses, given after a TPE session so it is not removed.

Caplacizumab (ISTH conditional, moderate certainty) when immune TTP is likely or confirmed: 10 mg IV before the first TPE, then 10 mg SC daily after each TPE and for 30 days after the last TPE. Access and cost limit use in India.

Do not give platelet transfusions unless there is life-threatening bleeding; they can worsen thrombosis. Central lines for TPE can be placed under ultrasound without platelet cover by experienced operators.

sections.title: Supportive care and special cases
items: Folic acid 5 mg daily; red cell transfusion for symptomatic anaemia.
Start LMWH thromboprophylaxis once platelets exceed 50 x 10^9/L.
Watch for TPE complications: line infection or thrombosis, citrate-related hypocalcaemia, and allergic reactions to plasma.
HIV-associated TTP: start antiretroviral therapy with specialist input. Pregnancy-associated TTP: joint haematology and obstetric care.
Congenital TTP: plasma infusion (10 to 15 mL/kg every 1 to 3 weeks) or, where available, recombinant ADAMTS13, which ISTH 2025 prefers for prophylaxis.

sections.title: Monitoring and response
items: Daily FBC, LDH, reticulocytes, renal function and neurological status; troponin if cardiac involvement.
Clinical response: platelets 150 x 10^9/L or more and LDH below 1.5 times the upper limit of normal.
Exacerbation is recurrence within 30 days of stopping TPE; relapse is recurrence after 30 days.
Measure ADAMTS13 weekly while on caplacizumab and extend caplacizumab while activity stays below 10 IU/dL. In remission, monitor ADAMTS13; rituximab prophylaxis is suggested if activity falls again.

sections.title: Escalate
items: ICU for neurological involvement, cardiac involvement (raised troponin, arrhythmia), AKI or haemodynamic instability.
Refractory disease (no platelet rise or worsening despite daily TPE and steroids): intensify therapy with rituximab and caplacizumab, and discuss with a tertiary TTP centre.
No local plasma exchange: arrange urgent transfer to a centre with apheresis while starting steroids and plasma infusion.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Transfusing platelets before the diagnosis is considered.
Delaying TPE while waiting for ADAMTS13 when probability is high, or forgetting to send ADAMTS13 before plasma.
Dismissing TTP because creatinine is normal or there is no fever or neurological sign.
Stopping caplacizumab while ADAMTS13 remains below 10 IU/dL, which risks exacerbation.
Mislabelling TTP as DIC (clotting is normal in TTP) or as malaria or sepsis.

drugs.name: Therapeutic plasma exchange
drugs.dose: 1.5 plasma volumes daily initially, then 1.0 plasma volume daily, with FFP or solvent-detergent plasma
drugs.notes: Start urgently; continue daily until platelet recovery under haematology guidance.

drugs.name: Methylprednisolone
drugs.dose: 1 g IV once daily for 3 days, then prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day orally with taper
drugs.notes: Alternatively prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day from the start.

drugs.name: Rituximab
drugs.dose: 375 mg/m2 IV once weekly for 4 doses
drugs.notes: Give after a TPE session. Screen for hepatitis B first.

drugs.name: Caplacizumab
drugs.dose: 10 mg IV before the first TPE, then 10 mg SC once daily after each TPE and for 30 days after the last TPE
drugs.notes: Extend while ADAMTS13 remains suppressed. Increases bleeding risk; hold before procedures.
